diagnostic_evidence.quote: (it actually holds for a slightly larger class of matrices)
we conjecture that the Hilbert structure is what enables the Eckart-Young-like results

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction says it shows that the scaled-unitary algebras are precisely the ones with Hilbert-algebra structure, which is an iff characterization. The paper proves only sufficiency, and for the larger class M = DW with D real diagonal, which strictly contains scaled unitaries. Necessity is never proved; the failure of the identity for other M is only asserted ('easy to build counter examples'). Eckart-Young is proved only for M = cW, and the paper itself says the link to the Hilbert structure is a conjecture. So the claimed explanation of why the scaled-unitary algebras are the right ones is not established.

failure_location.quote: We show that these tubal algebra are the ones that impose an Hilbert algebra structure

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim as a sufficient condition (M = DW satisfies the Hilbert-algebra identity), drop the 'are the ones' language, or prove the converse, and note that the class is larger than scaled unitaries.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised conceptual contribution of the last part (a characterization of the scaled-unitary algebras via Hilbert structure) is unsupported. The actual propositions are unaffected.
issues.title: Introduction claims scaled-unitary algebras are exactly those with Hilbert-algebra structure; only one direction (for a larger class) is shown
issues.why_classification: The repair is a rewording, but it withdraws the characterization claim, which is real mathematical content. The paper's formal results are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The same four equation hold if we replace $\va$ with $\matR_\va$, $\vy$ with $\matR_\vy$ and $\Mprod$ with matrix product.
However, the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse is unique, so $\matR_{\va^\winv}= \matR_\vy$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Penrose conditions require A A^+ and A^+ A to be symmetric. R_{a⋆y} = M^{-1} diag(0/1) M is an idempotent, but it is symmetric only if M is (essentially) scaled unitary. The ring-level third and fourth properties use the M-conjugate, not the matrix transpose. Counterexample: M=[[1,1],[0,1]] and a=(1,0) give R_a=[[1,1],[0,0]], which is its own weak inverse but not the pseudoinverse (1/2)[[1,0],[1,0]]. So the uniqueness step that forces a^- = y (hence a^- real) is invalid for general M. Lemma lem:winv-realness is stated for all admissible M.

failure_location.quote: Thus, $\matR_\vy$ is the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $\matR_\va$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pseudoinverse argument with a direct one. (Ma)^+ preserves the conjugate-pair structure because (conj z)^+ = conj(z^+). Then Lemma lem:struct-Minv (as in the proof of Lemma lem:added-14) shows M^{-1}(Ma)^+ is real. Alternatively, use uniqueness of the commutative von Neumann inverse inside the ring.
issues.overall_effect: Realness of a^- for general M is unproved, so the claim a^- ∈ K_M in lem:added-2 is unsupported as written. The lemma statement itself is true.
issues.title: Proof of real-valued weak inverse wrongly identifies R_y with the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse for general M
issues.why_classification: A few-line bypass using already-established lemmas fixes the proof, and the statement and all consequences survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since complex rows in $\matM$ come in pairs, the parity of the realness must be equal to the parity of $n$

issues.failure_explanation: The realness m can be any value n, n-2, ..., down to 0 or 1, which gives floor(n/2)+1 values, not ceil(n/2). For n=2 there are two values (m=2 split-complex, m=0 complex numbers), and the paper itself treats these as different tubal rings. For n=4 there are three values, not two. Also, Proposition prop:realness-iso proves only 'same realness implies isomorphic'; the count also needs 'different realness implies non-isomorphic', which is not shown.

failure_location.quote: thus there are, up to isomorphism, $\lceil \nicefrac{n}{2} \rceil$ tubal rings

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the count by floor(n/2)+1 and either prove or drop the claim that different realness gives non-isomorphic rings, for example by counting idempotents or real characters.
issues.overall_effect: The stated classification count is incorrect for even n and incompletely justified. The proposition itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Count of tubal rings up to isomorphism is wrong for even n and needs a converse not proved
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the count plus a short argument (or hedge) suffices. No formal result is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, it can be verified that weak inverses for non-zero elements are given by:

issues.failure_explanation: The first formula divides by a^2-b^2, which is zero when b=-a≠0, yet it is stated for all a≠b. The only degenerate case treated separately is a=b. Nonzero elements a(1-j) are therefore left without a stated weak inverse (it is [1/(4a); -1/(4a)]). The claim 'for non-zero elements' is not covered as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the first formula for a^2≠b^2 and add the case b=-a with weak inverse (1/(4a), -1/(4a)).
issues.overall_effect: The example's explicit description of weak inverses is incomplete and ill-defined on the line b=-a. The conclusion that the ring is tubal is unaffected.
issues.title: Weak-inverse formulas for split-complex numbers omit the case b = -a and are undefined there
issues.why_classification: A local degenerate-case fix; nothing else changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We can then move back to the primal domain to obtain \(\tenA = \tenU \Mprod \tenS \Mprod \tenV^\ha\).

issues.failure_explanation: U and V must lie in K_M^{m×m} and K_M^{p×p}, i.e. be real tensors. Mapping back by M^{-1} gives a real tensor only if the transformed faces have the conjugate-pair structure (faces for real rows of M real, faces for conjugate rows complex conjugates). Independent SVDs of each face give arbitrary unitary factors (phases, and complex factors even for real faces), so the back-transformed U, V need not be real. The proof never chooses conjugate-symmetric SVDs for paired faces or real SVDs for real faces.

failure_location.quote: Construct a SVD decomposition for each frontal slices on its own

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose SVDs of the paired faces as conjugates of each other (Â_k = conj(Â_j) gives U_k = conj(U_j) etc.) and real SVDs for faces from real rows of M. Then verify the conjugate-pair structure so U, S, V are real.
issues.overall_effect: Existence of an M-SVD with real, M-unitary factors is not established by the given proof. Results using that SVD inherit the gap.
issues.title: M-SVD construction ignores realness of U, V (conjugate-symmetric SVD choice)
issues.why_classification: A short, routine fix leaves the theorem and all dependents intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we write \(\va \Mleq \vb\) if \(\matM(\vb - \va)\) is real and element-wise non-negative

issues.failure_explanation: a ≥_M b only says â−b̂ ≥ 0 entrywise. If b̂ has negative entries the norm of b̂ can exceed that of â, e.g. â=(0,0), b̂=(−5,−5). The implication holds only when b ≥_M 0. The argument needs σ_{j+1} ≥_M 0, which is true but not invoked.

failure_location.quote: Clearly, for any two tubes \(\va\) and \(\vb\) of the same size \(\va \Mgeq \vb\) implies \(\Fnorm{\hat{\va}} \geq \Fnorm{\hat{\vb}}\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the implication to b ≥_M 0 and cite σ_{j+1} ≥_M 0 from the M-SVD theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification of the monotonicity of ||σ_j|| is invalid as written. The conclusion is true.
issues.title: False general ordering implication used in proof of Corollary (a ≥_M b does not imply ||â|| ≥ ||b̂||)
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis fix; the corollary stands.

issues.failure_explanation: Tensors are real (K_M^{m×p}), so the faces of B̂ for conjugate rows of M are complex conjugates and have equal rank. If r_j ≠ r_k for a conjugate pair (for example DFT rows j and n−j), the tensor [A]_r defined face-wise has non-conjugate faces. It is not a real tensor, and no real B has multirank ≤ r with those faces. The claimed optimal value and minimizer are then not attained within the stated class.

failure_location.quote: For any \(n\)-size tuple of non-negative integers \(\vr\) such that \(\vr \leq \Mmultirank(\tenA)\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis r_j = r_k whenever rows j,k of M are conjugate (and use conjugate-symmetric SVDs), or replace r_j by the minimum over the pair.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is false or ill-posed for tuples r not constant on conjugate pairs. It holds for symmetric tuples.
issues.title: Multirank Eckart–Young theorem allows truncation tuples not symmetric on conjugate pairs, giving non-real approximant and unattainable bound
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis restores the result with the same proof.

issues.failure_explanation: For M = cW the proof of lem:added-4 gives ||B||_F^2 = |c|^{-2} ||B̂||_F^2. The squared error is therefore |c|^{-2} times the sum of squared discarded transformed singular values. The stated factor |c|^{-1} is wrong whenever |c| ≠ 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |c|^{-1} by |c|^{-2}, as follows from lem:added-4.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit error value in the theorem is incorrect. The optimality assertion is unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong power of |c| in the error formula of the multirank Eckart–Young theorem
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction from an established lemma; no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that $\matM=\matD\matW$ for some invertible real diagonal matrix and unitary $\matW$.
however it is easy to build counter examples for which this does not hold

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the tensor identity reduces it, tube by tube, to the scalar identity <a⋆x,y> = <x,a^*⋆y> (the step '= Σ_j Σ_i <X_j, A_ij^* ⋆ Y_i>'). By the paper's own remark and prop:hilbert-algebra, this holds only for M = DW. The tensor proposition carries no such hypothesis, and with m=p=1 it reduces to the scalar identity, which fails for general M.

failure_location.quote: Suppose that $\tenA\in\KM^{m\times p}$. For every $\matX \in \KM^p$ and $\matY\in\KM^m$ we have

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis M = DW (D real invertible diagonal, W unitary) to the proposition.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition as stated is false for general M. It is valid under the M = DW hypothesis.
issues.title: Tensor Hilbert-algebra adjoint identity stated for all M but relies on the scaled-unitary hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the already-used hypothesis fixes the statement without changing the proof.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The use of complex numbers is unavoidable. It can be shown that no such real \(\matM\) exists.

issues.failure_explanation: The output contract demands a real M with op(x,y) = M^{-1}((Mx)⊙(My)). For tubal rings with complex rows (e.g. the C example, n=2, or any ring of realness < n) no real M exists. The algorithm computes M columns from eigenvalues of R_x, which are complex in general. The stated guarantee therefore cannot hold for those inputs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the output as M ∈ C^{n×n} (with the conjugate-pair row structure).
issues.overall_effect: The input-output contract is incorrect for every tubal ring that is not fully real.
issues.title: Algorithm for finding M declares a real matrix output, but M is generally complex
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction to the contract; the construction is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If we are dealing with a tubal ring Algorithm~\ref{alg:find-M} will find $\matM$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of prop:diag-is-Mprod uses a matrix S that jointly diagonalizes all R_a (from lem:diag-to-joint-diag). The algorithm instead takes an arbitrary eigendecomposition of one R_x. If R_x has a repeated eigenvalue, an arbitrary eigenbasis of that eigenspace does not diagonalize the other R_a, and the returned M would be wrong. For a tubal ring, generic x has distinct eigenvalues (the entries of Mx, since rows of M are distinct), but this is never argued. The claim 'will find M' is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the argument that for x outside a measure-zero set the eigenvalues of R_x are distinct, so its eigenbasis is unique up to scaling and diagonalizes every R_a. State the guarantee as holding almost surely.
issues.overall_effect: The stated guarantee of the algorithm is not proved. The statement should be 'with probability one over x'.
issues.title: Algorithm uses an eigenbasis of a single random R_x without justifying that it jointly diagonalizes all R_a
issues.why_classification: A short genericity argument closes the gap without changing the algorithm or its result.
